{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested (templated):
#   -P np01
#   -q normal
#   -N "{{:name}}"
#   -l ncpus={{:ncpus}}
#   -l mem={{:mem}}GB
#   -l walltime={{:wallhr}}:00:00
#   -j oe

flux alloc \
  -n {{:ncpus}} \
  --time={{:wallhr}}h \
  --queue=normal \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: PBS -P np01 (project/allocation) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: PBS -N "{{:name}}" (job name) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: PBS mem={{:mem}}GB has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# PBS -j oe (join stdout/stderr): approximate by redirecting stderr to stdout.
exec 2>&1

source $HOME/hpc-environments/gadi/load-intel.sh
PROJECT_DIR=$SCRATCH/{{:dir_name}}/

# NOTE: MPI launch integration is site-specific under Flux. We keep mpiexec as in the original.
# Performance implication: if mpiexec is not Flux-integrated on your system, ranks may not span resources as intended.
mpiexec -n {{:ncpus}} julia --project=$PROJECT_DIR --check-bounds no -O3 \
    $PROJECT_DIR/scripts/Benchmarks/benchmark_gadi.jl \
    {{:name}} \
    {{{:write_dir}}} \
    {{:type}} \
    {{:bmark_type}} \
    {{:Nx_partition}} \
    {{:Ny_partition}} \
    {{:Nz_partition}} \
    {{:n_el_size}} \
    {{:fe_order}} \
    {{:verbose}} \
    {{:nreps}}
'
"
}
